Error thrown when the anonymous session has expired or was rejected by Auth0, so no new

The stored anonymous session is deleted before this is thrown. Call

to start a new one. Any metadata attached to

Recovering from this is not free.

by creating a replacement anonymous identity rather than reporting the expiry, so by the

discards (storing it would move the visitor onto an identity they never asked for, without
their metadata). The

visitor actually needs a token on, rather than in a retry loop.

## Error Handling

The browser-facing auth routes (login, callback, and logout) forward failures to Express via
rather than writing error detail to the response themselves. Before doing so, the SDK replaces the underlying error with a sanitized one that carries only a generic message and a fixed

status. This has two effects:

- No internal detail (an OAuth
, a token-endpoint failure reason, stack traces, file paths) reaches the client, regardless of
. The original error is preserved on

, so your own logging can still inspect it.
- The failure status is a stable
instead of mirroring whatever status an upstream call happened to return (for example a

from the token endpoint).

Express still produces the final response. Its built-in error handler writes the (now generic) error stack into the response body unless

. For full control over what clients see, you can:

- Run your app with

in any deployed environment, and/or
- Mount your own [Express error-handling middleware](https://expressjs.com/en/guide/error-handling.html) after the Auth0 router. Read

there if you want to log the original failure.

The back-channel logout route is different: it is called server-to-server by Auth0, not by a browser, so the SDK owns its response directly and always replies with the status codes required by the [OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-backchannel-1_0.html) spec (a success status, which the SDK returns as
and the spec also allows as

on failure) without internal detail in the body. It does **not** flow through your error-handling middleware. If you need to log or customize back-channel logout failures, mount your own route and call
